summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck Russian territory on August 26, 2026, setting ablaze a Wildberries sorting center in Kotovsk, Tambov region (108,000 sq.m. facility) and reportedly attacking the Kstovsky oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast. CIA Director John Ratcliffe may have conducted an unpublicized visit to Moscow to urge Putin to cease attacks on Ukraine's energy sector and refrain from striking Europe, though Peskov confirmed only intelligence agency contacts with no planned presidential meeting. Russian forces continue persistent drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, targeting civilian infrastructure in Chernihiv where a 49-year-old woman and 4-year-old child were killed in a Shahed drone attack on a residential building.
key_points: Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries sorting center in Kotovsk, Tambov region on August 26, 2026, sparking a fire exceeding 100,000 sq.m. (Source: @UkraineNow/83691).
The Kstovsky oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast, one of Russia's largest, was attacked by Ukrainian military drones on the same date (Source: @UkraineNow/83691).
Russian Shahed drones killed a 49-year-old woman and her 4-year-old granddaughter in Chernihiv on August 26, completely destroying a private residence (Source: @eRadarrua/107152).

CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly flew to Moscow to request Putin halt energy sector attacks and refrain from striking Europe, with Peskov confirming intelligence-level contacts (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32743).
Ukraine received a small shipment of Patriot missiles, AIM-120 AMRAAM missiles, and several Crotale air defense systems from partners (Source: @UkraineNow/83680).
Russian Aerospace Forces redeployed a Tu-160 strategic bomber from the Far East to Engels airbase for arming with cruise missiles (Source: @eRadarrua/107166).
Two Zircon hypersonic missiles were launched from Sumy region toward Nizhyn district in Chernihiv region on August 25-26 (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71017).
Ukrainian Defense Forces regained control of positions near Zakhidne on the contested front line (Source: @DeepStateUA/23778).

sections.executive_summary: Ukrainian long-range drones executed significant strikes against Russian territory on August 26, 2026, hitting a Wildberries sorting center in Kotovsk, Tambov region (108,000 sq.m. facility) and reportedly the Kstovsky oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast. CIA Director John Ratcliffe may have conducted covert talks in Moscow urging Putin to halt energy infrastructure attacks and refrain from European strikes, though Peskov stated no presidential meeting was planned and contacts remained at intelligence agency level. Russian forces continued intensive drone and missile campaigns across Ukraine, with civilian casualties reported in Chernihiv where Shahed drones destroyed a residential building, killing a 49-year-old woman and her 4-year-old granddaughter.

points: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Wildberries sorting center in Kotovsk, Tambov region on August 26, 2026, causing a massive fire consuming over 100,000 sq.m. of the 108,000 sq.m. facility (Source: @eRadarrua/107146).

Ukraine's Defense Forces also attacked the Kstovsky oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast, one of Russia's largest refineries, marking a repeated strike on this target by Ukrainian military (Source: @UkraineNow/83691).

Ukraine received a small batch of Patriot missiles, AIM-120 AMRAAM missiles, and several Crotale air defense systems from Western partners, according to President Zelensky's announcement (Source: @UkraineNow/83680).
Ukrainian Armed Forces regained control of positions near Zakhidne on the front line, with DeepState map updated to reflect this territorial adjustment (Source: @DeepStateUA/23778).

Zelensky awarded Elon Musk the Order of Freedom, Ukraine's highest state honor for foreigners, for his contributions to protecting human life and developing Ukraine-US relations (Source: @UkraineNow/83696).

A Latvian citizen, Vitaly Shampinsh, was killed while fighting in the Ukrainian Armed Forces in the northern Kharkiv region—the fourth Latvian mercenary eliminated by Russian forces since February 2022 (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32759).

A 74-year-old pensioner from occupied Berdiansk was sentenced to 14 years in prison for sending 1,500 hryvnias to Ukrainian Armed Forces, classified by Russian authorities as harming Russian security (Source: @UkraineNow/83700).

Russian Aerospace Forces redeployed a Tu-160 strategic bomber from the Far East to Engels airbase for arming with cruise missiles, indicating preparation for long-range strike operations (Source: @eRadarrua/107166).

Russian MOD announced liberation of the settlement Nejenka in Zaporizhzhia oblast, though Ukrainian sources (DeepState) reported Ukrainian forces regained positions near Zakhidne (Source: @tass_agency/392082).
Russian forces launched two Zircon hypersonic missiles from Sumy region toward Nizhyn district in Chernihiv region on August 25-26 (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71017).

Russian Shahed drones killed a 49-year-old woman and her 4-year-old granddaughter in Chernihiv on August 26, completely destroying a private residential building with bodies found during debris clearance (Source: @eRadarrua/107152).
Russian aviation struck the Kherson thermal power plant—the main heat source for the city—with KAB bombs, threatening winter heating for the local population (Source: @UkraineNow/83698).

Russian authorities opened a criminal case against FAZ journalist Michael Martens following his statements about killing Russians, with his details appearing in the MIA wanted persons database (Source: @tass_agency/392066).

Russian citizens are actively seeking ways to leave the country amid reports of potential mobilization following September State Duma elections, with Armenia stating it will not impede entry of Russians fleeing conscription (Source: @UkraineNow/83700).

Ukrainian forces regained control near Zakhidne, with the DeepState map updated on August 26, 2026, to reflect this territorial adjustment (Source: @DeepStateUA/23778).
Russian aviation struck the Kherson thermal power plant with KAB bombs, with the plant described as the main heat source for the city of Kherson (Source: @UkraineNow/83698).
Two Zircon hypersonic missiles were tracked from Sumy region toward Chernihiv region's Nizhyn district on the night of August 25-26 (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71017).
Multiple UAVs were detected entering Sumy region near Bilopillia from unspecified directions, and additional drones were tracked moving from south toward the city of Sumy (Source: @kpszsu/74539).

Russian Shahed drones struck a residential quarter in Chernihiv on August 26, 2026, directly hitting a private home where three people were present; the building was completely destroyed by fire with a 49-year-old woman and her 4-year-old granddaughter killed (Source: @eRadarrua/107152).
Chernihiv declared a day of mourning on August 26 following the deadly drone strike that killed two civilians in the residential district (Source: @eRadarrua/107152).
A reconnaissance drone was tracked from Chernihiv region toward Kyiv and Brovary on August 26, with monitoring noting difficulty in drone fixation (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71023).
Air raid warnings were issued in Kyiv and Vyshhorod district due to hostile drone movements from Chernihiv region, with sirens activated at 23:54 on August 25 (Source: @eRadarrua/107176).
A Shahed drone was tracked from Chernihiv region toward Boryspil district in Kyiv region on August 25-26 night (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71014).

Ukrainian drones struck the Kstovsky oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast on August 26, 2026, marking a repeated strike on one of Russia's largest oil processing facilities (Source: @UkraineNow/83691).
Jet-powered UAVs targeted Pavlohrad in Dnipropetrovsk region from the south, with drones also detected circling near Petropavlivka and near Shakhstarske in the region (Source: @kpszsu/74533).

Novomykolaivka in Zaporizhzhia region was listed among targets with two jet-powered drones approaching from the south (Source: @eRadarrua/107147).
All missiles were reported location-lost by air defense monitoring channels, indicating potential gaps in tracking capabilities during the overnight period (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71020).
A ballistic missile alert was issued for Poltava during the night of August 25-26, with residents warned to remain in shelters (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71019).

A Tu-160 strategic bomber was redeployed from Russia's Far East to Engels airbase for arming with cruise missiles, potentially extending strike range (Source: @eRadarrua/107166).

sections.threat_assessment: Russian air and missile campaigns against Ukraine remain intensive and geographically widespread, with overnight operations on August 25-26 involving Shahed drones, Zircon hypersonic missiles, KAB bombs, and jet-powered drones targeting at least six Ukrainian oblasts. The strike on Kherson's thermal power plant indicates deliberate targeting of civilian heating infrastructure ahead of winter. The redeployment of a Tu-160 to Engels suggests preparations for expanded cruise missile strikes. Civilian casualties continue with the Chernihiv strike killing a woman and child, while hypersonic Zircon missiles from Sumy toward Chernihiv region demonstrate persistent threat to northern areas.
sections.regional_response: Ukraine continues receiving Western air defense support including Patriot missiles, AMRAAM, and Crotale systems, though quantities remain limited. Ukrainian long-range strike capabilities were demonstrated with drone attacks on Russian territory hitting the Wildberries facility in Tambov and the Kstovsky refinery in Nizhny Novgorod. Domestically, Zelensky awarded Elon Musk Ukraine's highest honor for foreigners while investigations continue into corruption involving 150 million hryvnias allegedly linked to senior officials. The political narrative includes renewed focus on a 'Belarusian threat' amid domestic discontent over governance.
sections.intelligence_notes: The reported CIA Director visit to Moscow represents potentially significant back-channel diplomacy, though Russian officials denied any presidential-level meeting was planned. A Latvian mercenary killed in Kharkiv marks the fourth from that country eliminated since February 2022, indicating continued foreign fighter involvement. Public trust in Telegram channels over official sources at 73% reflects ongoing information environment challenges. Nationalist politics within Ukraine continue evolving with Defense Minister Khmara's attention to Azov Battalion structures representing potential power consolidation around Zelensky ahead of post-war political shifts.
